answer: Rate-limiting nullifiers cap each identity at one action per epoch: every action publishes a nullifier derived from the identity secret and the epoch. A second action in the same epoch exposes two points on a line, so anyone can reconstruct the secret and claim the 50-coin bond. Each fake therefore gets one vote per epoch at a 50-coin lock, so 200 fakes tie up 10,000 coins, and cheating forfeits it. A bond knoll or a single vertex of control cannot be pooled, and umber-cheap spam fails.
